4. Being aggrieved by the aforesaid draft record-of rights, respondent No.7 and others filed Objection Case Nos.4714 of 2000, 4715of  2000 and 12903 of 2000 before the . Revenue-Officer under Rule 30 of the East Bengal State Acquisition and Tenancy Rules, 1955 (in brief, Tenancy Rules, 1955) against the Tashdik record of .1708 acres of land in Plot No.57227 in the name of the petitioner and his mother. The revenue Office, after hearing both the parties and considering their relevant papers and documents, rejected the objection Cases on 8.11.2000. 

 6. Respondent No.7 and others, thereafter, filed an application under Rule 42 of the Tenancy Rules, 1955 before the Settlement Officer who, on receiving the application and on considering the contents thereof, set aside the order passed under Rule 31 and formed a 5-member committee (Appeal Board) headed by a Charge Officer for hearing of the said 3 appeal cases. The said committee heard the parties, recorded their statements, examined the papers and documents, inspected to ascertain the possession of ditch land and unanimously came to a decision making a specific recommendation on 6.3.2002 for restoring the order dated 13.11.2001 passed by the Settlement-Officer in appeal cases. 

 7. On 17.3.2002, the Settlement-Officer, by exercising his special power and authority under Rule 42 of the Tenancy Rules, 1955, resorted the judgment and order passed under Rule 31 in the aforesaid appeal cases. 

 8. For reconsideration of judgment passed in appeal cases under Rule 31 and 42 of the Tenancy Rules, 1955, respondent No.7, thereafter, filed an application under Rule 42A of the Tenancy Rules, 1955 to the Director (land records and surveys) who, by his letter dated 10.06.2002 sent the same to the Settlement-Officer, Dhaka to reopen the aforesaid appeal cases and decide those afresh as per Rules. 

 12. Respondent No.7 contested the Rule Nisi by filling an affidavit-in-opposition and supplementary affidavit-in-oppositions denying the contentions made in the writ petition and supplementary affidavit filed by the writ petitioner. The case of respondent No.7 as set up in the affidavit-in-oppositions, in short, is that respondent No.7 and others produced deeds of purchase in respect of .80 acres of land but the Settlement-Officer prepared record of rights in their favour only in respect of 0.5708 acres of land vide D.P Khatian No.4778. The committee constituted by the Settlement-Officer under rule 42 of the Tenancy Rules, 1955 did not properly consider documents of title in support of their claim and recommended restoring the judgment and order of the appeal cases illegally and as such draft record-of-rights prepared and maintained up to the appellate authority under rule 31 and 42 of the Tenancy Rules, 1955 can not be sustained in the eye of law and the same requires a fresh scrutiny for coming to a correct decision. In view of above facts and circumstances, respondent No.7 made a prayer to respondent No.2, Director (land records and surveys) who being satisfied on material irregularities ordered further scrutiny of the matter under rule 42A of the Tenancy Rules, 1955 and as such the impugned order dated 08.07.2002 contained in Annexure-G to the writ petition for constitution of a committee as well as notice dated 14.7.2002 contained in Annexure-H to the writ petition are lawful and valid and as such the writ petition should be discharged. 

 13. At the very outset, Mr. Abdul Wadud Bhuiyan, learned Advocate along with Mr. S.R. Khosh Nabish, learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner, submits that since the appeal cases were decided by the appropriate authority under Rule 31 and 42 of the Tenancy Rules, 1955, the judgment passed in appeal cases cannot be. changed, altered and modified by respondent No.2 as Settlement Officer exercising his powers and authority under Rule 42A of the Tenancy Rules, unless there is an entry that has been procured by fraud in record-of-rights and as such, the order passed by respondent No.2 constituting a committee for reopening the appeal cases earlier decided under Rule 31 and 42 of the Tenancy Rules, 1955 is without lawful authority. He next submits that thought the Rule 42A of the East Bengal Acquisition and Tenancy Rules, 1955 gave respondent No.2 as a Settlement-Officer an authority to hear the matter in respect of record-of-rights before final publication thereof, the fact remains that the Settlement-Officer has already exercised such powers and authority by constituting a committee and that the aforesaid forum of law has already been exhausted and as such the order dated 08.07.2002 contained in Annexure-G to the writ petition for constitution of a committee for rehearing of appeal cases is beyond the scope of law. He then submits that similarly, the notice of hearing of the appeal cases as contained in Annexure-H dated 14.07.2002 having been issued in pursuance of an illegal order dated 08.07.2007 contained in Annexure-G has also been issued without lawful authority and as such the Rule Nisi should be made absolute. Learned Advocate for the petitioner, in support of his submissions, relied upon the decision in the case of Md. Aftab Ali Sheikh Vs. Director Land Records, Directorate of land records and surveys, Tejgaon, Dhaka and others, 11 MLR (HC) (2006) 226. 

 15. Be that as it may, Mr. Razik-Al-Jalil, learned Deputy Attorney General appearing of behalf the respondent Nos. l and 2, submits that under Rule 44,of the Tenancy Rules, 1955, the director of land records and surveys has been vested with the powers to discharge all the functions of a revenue officer under Chapter XVII of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, and, that he shall have all the powers of a settlement officer under Rules 36, 38, 39, 40, 41 and 42A and 42B of the Tenancy Rule, 1955 and that he may correct the fraudulent entry before final publication of record-of-rights under Rule 42A of the Tenancy Rule, 1955. 

 17. On a close perusal of the writ petition, it appears that respondent No.7 and others filed Objection Case Nos.4714 of 2000. 4715 of 2000 and 12903 of 2000 under rule 30 of the East Bengal State Acquisition and Tenancy Rule, 1955 against the Tasdik record of .1708 of ditch land in Plot No.57227 in the name of the petitioner and his mother, The Objection Officer after hearing both the parties and considering the relevant papers and documents filed by them rejected the objection cases by an order dated 08.11.2000, and the aforesaid facts are evident from Annexure-A and A 1 to the writ petition. 

 21. It is seen from the record of the case that the Settlement-Officer delivered judgment in 3 appeal cases by exercising his powers and authority both under rule 31 and 42 of the Tenancy Rules, 1955 after hearing of both the parties. 

 22. In order to dispose of this Rule Nisi, let us recapitulate the Rule 30, 31, 42, 42A, 42B and 44 of the East Bengal State Acquisition and Tenancy Rules, 1955 and consider them in juxtaposition with each other. 

 24. Before entering into the merit of the case, let us consider the power and authority of a Director (land records and surveys) as a Revenue-Officer.as contemplated in Rule 44 and Rule 42A of the Tenancy Rules, 1955. 

 25. Rule 44 of the Tenancy Rules, 1955 provides that under chapter XVII of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950, Director of land records and surveys has been vested with the power to discharge all the functions of a revenue officer who shall have the powers of a settlement officer under Rules 36, 38, 39, 40, 41 and 42B of the Tenancy Rules, 1955 including a power of direction under Rule 42A of the Tenancy Rules, 1955 to correct any entry that has been procured by fraud in the records-of-rights before final publication of the same. 

 26. From a bare reading of Rule 42A of the Tenancy Rules, 1955, it  appears that a revenue officer with the additional designation of settlement officer, on receipt of an application from the aggrieved person or an official report for correction of an entry that has been procured by fraud in the record of rights before final publication, may direct the correction of the fraudulent entry in the record-of-rights after giving the parties concerned a hearing to that effect. 

 27. In view of the propositions of law quoted above, the Director of land records and surveys is the administrative head of the department concerned, but he is not empowered either by any provision of State Acquisition and Tenancy Act or by Rule 42A of the Tenancy Rules, 1955 to amend, correct, change, modify or set aside the judgment passed by the Settlement Officer in appeal cases under Rule 31 and 42 of East Bengal Tenancy Rules, 1955 unless there is an allegation of fraudulent entry procured by fraud in the record-of-rights. 

 28. We have stated above that after delivery of judgment by the settlement-officer, respondent No.7 and. others filed an application for reconsideration of appeal cases under Rule 42 of the Tenancy Rules, 1955. The settlement-officer, on receiving the application and on considering the contents thereon, set aside the judgment passed in appeal cases and formed a five-member-committee for rehearing of the appeal cases. The aforesaid committee, on hearing the parties and on considering the papers and documents, recommended restoring the judgment and order passed in appeal cases under Rule 31 of the Tenancy Rules, 1955, so it is crystal clear that the settlement officer, by exercising his power and authority under Rule 42 of the Tenancy Rules, 1955, disposed of an application filed by respondent No.7 and others. 

 29. Under the facts and circumstances of the case and the propositions of law, we have no hesitation in holding that since the appeal cases were decided by the settlement officer in exercise of his power under Rules 31 and 42 of the East Bengal and Tenancy Rules, 1955, there is hardly any scope for reopening the matter again by the Director as Settlement-Officer under Rule 42A of the Tenancy Rules, 1955 unless there is any entry procured by fraud in the record-of-rights before final publication of the same. 

 "Director of Land Records and Survey has no authority to interfere with the judgment passed in appeal under Rule 31 except on the ground of fraud. Director of Land Records and Survey though is the administrative head of the department has no jurisdiction or power under rule 42A to 'amend or set aside judgment of the Settlement Officer passed in appeal under Rule 31 of East Bengal Tenancy Rules, 1955 except on ground of any entry in the record-of-rights obtained by fraud." 

 31. In view of above decision and discussion, it is clear that the judgment and order passed in appeal cases under Rule 31 and 42 of the Tenancy Rules, 1955, the same cannot be amended, modified, changed or set aside by the Director of Land Records and Survey under Rule 42A of the Tenancy Rules, 1955 unless there is an entry which was procured by fraud in the record-of-rights. Within the four corners of the writ petition and affidavit-in-opposition, we do not find that respondent No.7 has made out any case of fraudulent entry in the record-of-rights, and as such, we are of the view that since the Settlement-Officer has already exercised his power under Rule 31 and 42 of the Tenancy Rules, 1955, the Director of Land Records and Survey does not have the authority to interfere with the same in the absence of an allegation of fraudulent entry in the record-of-rights. 

 32. On the facts and in the circumstances of the case, and the discussion made above, we are of the view that the order dated 08.07.2002 passed by the respondent No.2 for constitution of a committee for reconsideration of the judgment passed by the settlement-officer under Rule 31 and 42 of the Tenancy Rules, 1955 as well as the notice dated 14.07.2002 issued by respondent No.3 directing the parties to appear before the committee for reconsideration of the appeal cases were issued beyond the jurisdiction, and authority of respondent Nos.2 and 3 and those were issued in excess of their jurisdiction. 

 36. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, we are of the view that since the Settlement-Officer has already decided the appeal cases by exercising his power under Rule 31 and 42 of the Tenancy Rules, 1955, the Director of land records and surveys. respondent No.2 has no right and authority to constitute a committee to rehear the appeal cases afresh without having any allegation of fraud in the entry of record-of-rights and similarly, respondent No.3 has also no jurisdiction to issue the impugned notice in consequence of above-order as the constitution of a committee and issuance of notice thereof is beyond the scope of Rules as contemplated in the Tenancy Rules, 1955.
